name: PRISM
tagline: See how the world sees your professional brand.
audience: Mid-to-senior professionals, founders, consultants, and anyone seeking to understand and enhance their professional market positioning
delivery_format: 30-question self-assessment, instant report with archetype profile
outcome_statement: A clear picture of your professional brand across five dimensions, your personal brand archetype (one of ten), and specific, actionable steps to strengthen your market visibility and positioning.
use_cases: Self-assessment for professionals building their personal brand
Career transition and job search preparation

scoring_framework.method: Five-dimension brand profile with archetype mapping via 2×2 matrix (Visibility × Consistency)
scoring_framework.archetype_detection: 10 real archetypes positioned on a 2-axis grid (Visibility × Consistency/Narrative)
scoring_framework.response_scale: 5-point Likert — Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree
matrix_axes: Axis 2: Brand Consistency / Narrative Alignment (diffuse → focused)
scoring_framework.important_note: Axis 1 and Axis 2 are structural positioning axes, NOT archetypes. They define the grid on which the 10 archetypes sit.

dimensions.name: Brand Clarity
dimensions.description: How clearly defined and articulated your professional brand identity is — do you know what you stand for and can you articulate it?

dimensions.name: Market Legibility
dimensions.description: How easily your target audience can understand what you do, what value you offer, and where you fit in the market.

dimensions.name: Identity Consistency
dimensions.description: How consistent your brand is across channels, contexts, and interactions — does your LinkedIn match your in-person presence match your work output?

dimensions.name: Narrative Power
dimensions.description: How compelling and memorable your professional story is — can you communicate your value in a way that resonates and sticks?

dimensions.name: Visibility Level
dimensions.description: How visible you are to your target audience — both in terms of presence in relevant spaces and recognition for your expertise.

archetypes.name: The Authority
archetypes.summary: Established expert with a clear, consistent brand that's widely recognized in their field.
archetypes.growth_area: Avoiding stagnation — continuous reinvention without losing identity

archetypes.name: The Signal
archetypes.summary: Highly visible professional whose brand cuts through the noise, though the message may be scattered.
archetypes.strengths: Visibility, reach, ability to get attention

archetypes.name: The Monument
archetypes.summary: Well-known but with a brand that feels dated, static, or misaligned with current goals.

archetypes.name: The Chameleon
archetypes.summary: Adaptable professional with a strong but context-dependent brand — fits in everywhere but lacks a distinct signature.

archetypes.name: The Amplifier
archetypes.summary: Solid professional brand with good visibility and growing clarity — on the cusp of breaking through.
archetypes.growth_area: Narrowing focus and doubling down on what works

archetypes.name: The Operator
archetypes.summary: Competent behind-the-scenes operator whose brand doesn't match their actual capability.

archetypes.name: The Ghost
archetypes.summary: Clear, consistent brand that almost no one sees — high substance, low visibility.

archetypes.name: The Mask
archetypes.summary: Professional whose public persona feels like a performance — careful, controlled, but not fully authentic.

archetypes.name: The Static
archetypes.summary: Brand is scattered and hard to see — mixed signals across channels and no clear positioning.
archetypes.growth_area: Everything — start with clarity, then build visibility

archetypes.name: The Blank Page
archetypes.quadrant: Very Low Visibility, Very Low Consistency
archetypes.summary: Early-stage professional or career changer who hasn't yet built a defined professional brand.
archetypes.growth_area: Foundational brand definition and first visibility steps

matrix_structure.note: The 2×2 matrix has been expanded to a more nuanced 3×3 grid (Visibility × Consistency), creating 9 cells with 10 archetypes (one archetype — The Blank Page — sits below the grid for very early-stage).

pillar_mapping.relationship: PRISM supports individual leaders in building their personal brand and market positioning, which feeds into organizational impact and board-level visibility
cross_pillar_relevance: P1 Talent Pipeline Health — personal branding supports career advancement and pipeline velocity
P2 Cross-Border Leadership Effectiveness — brand legibility is critical for cross-border leaders

key_methodological_notes: 10 real archetypes on a 3×3 grid (plus 1 below-grid = The Blank Page)
Axis 1 and Axis 2 are structural grid axes, NOT archetypes — they should not appear in archetype lists or count toward archetype total
Self-report assessment — measures self-perceived brand, not external perception
Report includes dimension radar chart, archetype profile, and development recommendations

naming_origin.reason: 'Legibility' is a single dimension (D2 Market Legibility), not the whole product. The product covers the full professional branding system — clarity, legibility, consistency, narrative, and visibility.

provenance.dimensions: prism_config.json + PRISM_QB_notion.json — 5 dimensions validated across both sources
provenance.archetypes: prism_config.json — 12 entries total; 2 are matrix axes (Axis 1, Axis 2) and 10 are real archetypes
provenance.archetype_grid_structure: Inferred from archetype name semantics — 3×3 visibility × consistency grid
